title: AutoGen — AgentChat and Core
intro: The familiar layer, then the genuinely different idea underneath.

steps.title: AgentChat: deliberately familiar
steps.body: Three concepts — **Model, Message, Agent** — driven with `on_messages`. The lab builds a ticket-price assistant with a local database tool. If it feels like Crew and the Agents SDK, that's the point the course makes explicitly.

steps.title: Core: the different idea
steps.body:
> [!key] **AutoGen Core decouples an agent's logic from how messages are delivered.** The framework provides the communication infrastructure — a **Runtime** — plus agent lifecycle; agents are responsible only for their own work.

Core is framework-agnostic: you can run AgentChat agents on it, or anything else. The course positions it "similarly to LangGraph" — an interaction substrate, not an agent library.

steps.title: The stack
steps.body: Three layers, each answering a different question — what agents say, how messages move, and where the processes run:

points.label: AgentChat
points.note: High-level, conversation-first: Model + Message + Agent, on_messages. Group chats coordinate by talking.

points.label: Core
points.note: Runtime owns message delivery + lifecycle; agent logic never knows the transport.

points.label: Distributed
points.note: The same Core abstractions across processes and machines — the runtime becomes a distributed message fabric.

steps.title: Choosing chat as coordination
steps.body:
Conversation-based coordination (group chats, speaker selection) is the most **flexible** and least **predictable** model in the course's taxonomy — suited to brainstorm-shaped, open-ended collaboration; risky where a step must never be skipped (that's a graph's job).

> [!tip] The four frameworks in one line each: **SDK** — you orchestrate, agents work. **Crew** — org chart. **LangGraph** — state machine. **AutoGen** — conversation over a runtime.

recap:
**AgentChat is the familiar face; the Runtime is the idea.**

- Model + Message + Agent + on_messages.
- Core: delivery and lifecycle are infrastructure; agents only do their work.
- Distributed = same abstractions across machines.
- Chat coordination for open-ended work; graphs where steps are guaranteed.
